tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Daawid's open registry of people, businesses and organizations by what the user needs, such as 'a dentist in Nairobi' or 'a CRM for a small team'. Each result says who it is, where, and whether it takes on work; get_entry shows one to the user, get_entry_sections reads parts of one.

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: Show the user one whole entry of Daawid's registry, by its ID, slug or a website its owner proved control of (`domain`): what it offers with prices, whether it takes on work, hours, contact details, policies and legal details, as its owner declared them. Apps show it as a card. Not needed before a r

tools.name: get_entry_sections
tools.description: Read only some parts of an entry, with no card: its actions before a request, say, or its hours. To show the user the entry, use get_entry.

tools.name: get_offerings
tools.description: List what one entry of Daawid's registry offers, with prices and lead times, as its owner declared them: all of it, or what matches a few words, a category or an audience.

tools.name: get_brand_kit
tools.description: Get one entry's brand kit, as its owner declared it: logo, pictures, colours, fonts and corners. For showing or building something in the entry's own look.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Ask an entry for a quote for the user: a price for a job they describe. Only for entries whose actions (get_entry_sections) list request_quote. Ask the user for their name and email address, and add a budget only if they give one. Nothing is sent by this call: the user sends it on Daawid's page, wit

tools.name: request_callback
tools.description: Ask an entry to call the user back, about what they want to talk about, at times that suit them. Only for entries whose actions (get_entry_sections) list request_callback. Ask the user for their name, email address and phone number. Nothing is sent by this call: the user sends it on Daawid's page, w

tools.name: request_appointment
tools.description: Ask an entry for an appointment for the user, such as a visit, a consultation or a demo. It is a request: the entry's owner confirms a time, or suggests another. Only for entries whose actions (get_entry_sections) list request_appointment. Ask the user for their name and email address. Nothing is se

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an entry for the user: a question, or anything they want its owner to know. Only for entries whose actions (get_entry_sections) list send_message. Ask the user for their name and email address. Nothing is sent by this call: the user sends it on Daawid's page, with a code Daawid ema

tools.name: get_request_status
tools.description: Check where a request made through Daawid is: waiting for the user on Daawid's page, sent, delivered or opened. It never shows what the request says or who sent it.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_quote, request_callback, request_appointment, send_message · Private data: get_entry · Public sink: request_quote, request_callback, request_appointment, send_message.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_quote, request_callback, request_appointment, send_message · Private data: get_entry · Public sink: request_quote, request_callback, request_appointment, send_message

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
